The CBC reveals significant pancytopenia with a very high white blood cell count of 81,000/mm³, suggesting a problem with white blood cell maturation rather than just nutritional deficiency. speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood smear showing immature cells with prominent nucleoli and pink, needle-shaped inclusions is highly characteristic of the Auer rods seen in acute leukemia. Given your pancytopenia and these specific findings, have you experienced any night sweats, fevers, or significant bone pain recently?

REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The bone marrow biopsy results showing normal readings contradict the previous findings of Auer rods and acute leukemia. To clarify this discrepancy and confirm the presence of immature cells or blasts, I need to review the microscopic images of the biopsy and the original blood smear.

speaker: Patient
text: 67-year-old male. The patient complains of a 2-month history of generalized fatigue. He mentions no specific triggers but notes that the fatigue has been progressively worsening. He denies any recent infections, significant weight loss, or night sweats.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL). The clinical presentation of pancytopenia combined with the specific finding of cells containing needle-shaped Auer rods on the peripheral smear is pathognomonic for this subtype of acute myeloid leukemia, despite the conflicting bone marrow biopsy result. The absence of fever or night sweats does not rule out this diagnosis, which is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment with all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA).
